name: RACV Cape Schanck Resort
address: Trent Jones Drive, Cape Schanck VIC 3939
description: Taxi to RACV Cape Schanck Resort for golf weekends, weddings and coastal stays. Airport transfers and wheelchair taxis on the southern peninsula.
entrance: We pull up at the main hotel entrance, where guests check in at reception.
spot: Drop-off and pick-up are at the front of the resort building; for functions or the golf clubhouse, tell us when you book and we will meet you at the door you name.
parking: After a wedding reception or a long lunch with drinks, a taxi means nobody has to drive the dark, winding roads around Cape Schanck.
access: Let us know if anyone needs the wheelchair van or help with luggage, and ask the resort about step-free routes to your room.
tips: Add your flight number when booking an airport transfer so we can track delays on the way back to the resort.
Book wedding-night return trips well before the day, as late pick-ups at Cape Schanck need to be planned.
Golfers with clubs should mention them so we send a vehicle with enough boot space.
about: RACV Cape Schanck Resort sits on a golf course near the southern tip of the Mornington Peninsula, with views across the dunes towards Bass Strait. It is a popular base for golf breaks, conferences, family holidays and weddings, and it is a fair way from the nearest train line, so most guests arrive by car or taxi.

We drive guests to and from the resort at all hours. Common trips include Melbourne Airport transfers, rides to cellar doors in Red Hill and Main Ridge, and late returns after dinner in Sorrento or Rye. Wedding parties often book several cars so guests staying in Rosebud, Mornington or Frankston can get home without working out who stays sober. Golfers often split the day, with a morning round on the resort course and an afternoon at a cellar door, and a taxi makes that second half far more relaxing.

If you travel with a wheelchair or a mobility scooter, our wheelchair accessible van carries one chair plus four seated passengers, and the Maxi WAT takes two wheelchairs and six others. Book ahead for summer weekends and golf events, when the southern peninsula is at its busiest.

faq.q: Can you pick us up from Melbourne Airport and take us straight to the resort?
faq.a: Yes. Book online or by phone and include your flight number, and we track the flight so the pick-up time moves if you land early or late. Let us know how many bags and whether you have golf clubs, so we send a sedan or a larger vehicle with enough room for everyone and everything.

faq.q: We are going to a wedding at the resort. Can you get guests home afterwards?
faq.a: We can. Book the return times in advance, ideally a little after the reception is due to finish, and give us the addresses guests are heading to. For bigger groups the Maxi WAT seats up to eight, or six seated plus two wheelchairs, which suits guests sharing a ride back to the same town.

name: Jackalope Hotel
description: Book a taxi to Jackalope Hotel in Merricks North for dinners, stays and airport transfers. Sedans and wheelchair accessible taxis available 24/7.
entrance: We drop you at the hotel’s main arrival area beside the vineyard; tell us if you are heading to one of the restaurants rather than reception.
spot: Pick-up is at the front of the hotel. If you are dining at the Willow Creek cellar door or restaurant on the same property, let us know which building you will be at.
parking: Dinner at Jackalope usually comes with a wine list worth exploring, and a taxi home lets everyone in your party enjoy it.
access: Tell us if you need the wheelchair van, and check with the hotel about level paths between the buildings on the estate.
tips: The hotel shares its site with Willow Creek Vineyard, so you can pair a tasting with your stay without another trip.
Balnarring Road is dark at night; book your return pick-up time before you sit down to dinner.
Arriving from the airport late? Add your flight number so we can adjust if your plane is delayed.
about: Jackalope Hotel is a boutique design hotel set among the vines of Willow Creek Vineyard in Merricks North, in the hills between Red Hill and Balnarring. It draws guests for its architecture, its dining and its quiet rural setting, and it is a regular choice for special-occasion stays and celebrations.

Because it sits on a country road with no public transport close by, a taxi is the simplest way in and out. We take guests from Melbourne Airport and Frankston station, run diners from Mornington and Mount Martha out for a long dinner, and bring them home afterwards. Couples staying the night often book us to explore nearby cellar doors in Red Hill and Merricks the next day. Hotel guests heading out for dinner in Flinders, Red Hill or Mornington can book a return trip so the evening ends back at their room without anyone behind the wheel.

Our sedans suit couples and small groups. If someone in your party uses a wheelchair, the accessible van has a rear ramp and four-point restraints, and the Maxi WAT can carry two wheelchairs alongside six seated passengers. Weekend evenings book out quickly in summer, so reserve early.

faq.q: Is there public transport to Jackalope Hotel?
faq.a: Not in any practical sense for most visitors. The hotel is on Balnarring Road in a rural area, so guests usually drive or come by taxi. We can collect you from Frankston station, a peninsula address or Melbourne Airport and bring you to the door, then take you home again whenever you are ready.

faq.q: Can you take us from Jackalope to other wineries during our stay?
faq.a: Yes. Many guests book us for a short loop of nearby cellar doors in Red Hill, Merricks and Main Ridge. Tell us which wineries you plan to visit and roughly how long you will stay at each, and we can set up the pick-ups so you are not waiting around between tastings.

name: Lindenderry at Red Hill
address: 142 Arthurs Seat Road, Red Hill VIC 3937
description: Taxi to Lindenderry at Red Hill for weddings, country house stays and long lunches. Wheelchair taxis and return trips available any time.
entrance: We follow the driveway up to the main house and drop you at the front entrance near reception.
spot: Drop-off and pick-up are outside the main building; for weddings or events in the gardens, tell us where guests are gathering and we will come to the closest point a car can reach.
parking: Wedding guests at Lindenderry can relax and toast the couple properly when a taxi is booked to take them home.
access: Some garden areas include lawns and slopes, so let us know if anyone needs a hand, and ask the venue about the easiest route to your event space.
tips: For weddings, book all guest return trips together so cars arrive in sequence rather than all at once.
Combine a stay with visits to Red Hill cellar doors close by on Arthurs Seat Road and Red Hill Road.
Red Hill can get foggy and dark at night; agree a pick-up time and we will be there.
about: Lindenderry at Red Hill is a country house hotel with its own vineyard, set in landscaped gardens on Arthurs Seat Road. It is well known on the peninsula as a wedding and function venue, as well as a place for weekend escapes and long lunches in the hinterland.

Most of our Lindenderry bookings are tied to an occasion. We pick up wedding guests from accommodation in Dromana, Rosebud and Mornington, run the bridal party between photo spots, and handle the late trips home when the dancing finishes. Hotel guests also book us for Melbourne Airport transfers, which we time around your flight with live tracking. Couples staying for the weekend also use us to reach nearby cellar doors and, on market days, the Red Hill Community Market just up the road.

Our wheelchair accessible van and Maxi WAT mean older relatives and guests with mobility needs can arrive in the same convoy as everyone else. The Maxi WAT seats up to six with two wheelchairs, which is handy for families travelling together. Spring and summer Saturdays are the peak for weddings in Red Hill, so book as soon as you have your timings.

faq.q: Can you organise transport for a whole wedding party at Lindenderry?
faq.a: We can help with multiple cars for arrivals and departures. Send us the pick-up addresses, the number of guests and any wheelchair users, plus the ceremony and finish times. We will suggest a mix of sedans, the wheelchair van and the Maxi WAT so everyone is covered, with confirmations sent by SMS or email.

faq.q: How late can we book a pick-up from Lindenderry?
faq.a: We run 24 hours, seven days, so a pick-up after midnight is fine. Late trips in the hills are best booked ahead rather than on the night, so we can have a car committed to your time. If the event runs over, call us and we will adjust where we can.

name: Peppers Moonah Links Resort
description: Taxi to Peppers Moonah Links Resort in Fingal for golf stays, hot springs trips and airport transfers. Sedans and wheelchair taxis, 24/7.
entrance: We drop you at the resort’s main reception entrance; golfers heading to the clubhouse can ask to be taken there instead.
spot: Pick-ups are from the front of reception. If you are staying in a room block further from the entrance, tell us and we will meet you as close as the driveway allows.
parking: Ending a golf day with drinks at the clubhouse is easier when nobody has to drive back to Melbourne.
access: Let us know about wheelchairs, walkers or heavy luggage when booking so we can send the right vehicle.
tips: The resort is close to Peninsula Hot Springs and Alba Thermal Springs, which makes for an easy short taxi hop.
Mention golf bags when you book so the vehicle has room for them.
Summer and school holidays are busy around Fingal and Rye; book your return trip early.
about: Peppers Moonah Links Resort is a hotel set within the Moonah Links golf estate at Fingal, among the sand dunes and coastal scrub between Rye and Cape Schanck. Golfers come for the two championship courses on site, while other guests use it as a quiet base for the hot springs, the back beaches and the wineries further east.

We regularly take guests between the resort and Melbourne Airport, Frankston station or homes across the south-east. The resort is also a short ride from both thermal bathing venues in Fingal, so we often run guests over for a morning soak and back for lunch. Conference groups and golf days book several cars at a time. Families staying over the school holidays use us for trips to the back beaches at Gunnamatta and St Andrews, and into Rye for supplies.

If you travel with a wheelchair, our accessible van has a rear ramp and room for four other passengers, and the Maxi WAT carries up to two wheelchairs plus six seated passengers with a hydraulic hoist. Booking ahead is wise in summer, when taxis on the southern peninsula are in high demand.

faq.q: Can you take us from Peppers Moonah Links to Peninsula Hot Springs?
faq.a: Yes, it is one of our most common short trips from the resort. Book a drop-off time that suits your bathing session and a return time for when you expect to finish. If you are not sure how long you will stay, ask about calling us when ready, though a set time is more reliable on busy weekends.

faq.q: Do you have vehicles big enough for a golf group?
faq.a: Our Maxi WAT carries up to eight seated passengers, or fewer with wheelchairs on board, and sedans suit smaller groups. Tell us how many players and golf bags you have when booking, and we will suggest the best combination of vehicles so clubs and passengers fit comfortably.

name: InterContinental Sorrento Mornington Peninsula
description: Taxi to InterContinental Sorrento on Ocean Beach Road for stays, weddings and dinners. Airport transfers and wheelchair accessible taxis available.
entrance: We stop at the hotel’s main entrance on Ocean Beach Road in the Sorrento village strip.
spot: Drop-off and pick-up are at the front of the hotel. Ocean Beach Road can be congested in summer, so we may stop a few metres along from the door if the kerb is busy.
parking: Sorrento’s main street is crowded with cars in summer, and a taxi spares you the search for a park near the hotel.
access: Tell us if you need the wheelchair van or help with bags, and check with the hotel about step-free entry to the area you are visiting.
tips: Coming off the Queenscliff ferry? We can meet you near the Sorrento terminal and run you up to the hotel.
Book a fixed time for returns after weddings or functions, as summer nights in Sorrento are very busy.
Add your flight number for airport transfers so we can follow any delays.
about: The InterContinental Sorrento occupies the restored limestone Continental Hotel on Ocean Beach Road, right in the middle of Sorrento village. Alongside its rooms it has bars, dining and event spaces, and it hosts weddings and functions throughout the year.

Guests use our taxis to arrive from Melbourne Airport or Frankston, to get to back beach walks and Point Nepean, and to visit wineries in Red Hill without worrying about driving. Event guests often stay in Rye, Rosebud or Blairgowrie and book us to bring them in for the evening and home again afterwards. Sorrento village is compact, but the peninsula around it is spread out, with wineries, golf courses and hot springs all a drive away. Booking a taxi for those outings lets guests make the most of a stay without moving the car or deciding who drives.

We offer sedans for everyday trips and two kinds of wheelchair accessible vehicle for guests with mobility needs: a van with a rear ramp, and a Maxi WAT with a hydraulic hoist that suits heavier power chairs. Carers travel with the passenger. Summer and long weekends are the peak in Sorrento, so book well ahead.

faq.q: Can you meet us at the Sorrento ferry and take us to the hotel?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us which ferry you are on and roughly when it is due in, and we will arrange a pick-up near the Sorrento terminal. It is a short run up to Ocean Beach Road, which saves carrying luggage through the village. Let us know if anyone needs the wheelchair van.

faq.q: We are attending a function at the hotel. Can you take us home late at night?
faq.a: We operate around the clock, so late returns are no trouble. Book your pick-up time in advance and tell us where everyone is going. If guests are heading in different directions, we can send separate cars, or one larger vehicle if you are all going the same way.

name: Hotel Sorrento
description: Taxi to Hotel Sorrento on Hotham Road for bayside stays, pub meals and events. Book a sedan or wheelchair accessible taxi day or night.
entrance: We drop you at the front of the hotel on Hotham Road, a short walk up from the Sorrento foreshore.
spot: Pick-up is outside the hotel on Hotham Road. If you are staying in the hotel’s apartments, tell us so we can meet you at the most convenient door.
parking: On a sunny weekend, parking around Sorrento fills fast, and a taxi to the door saves circling the block after a meal and a drink.
access: Hotham Road runs uphill from the water, so let us know if anyone would prefer to be dropped right at the door rather than walking from the foreshore.
tips: Pair a lunch here with a stroll down to the foreshore and pier, then book a pick-up from the hotel later.
If you are coming in on the ferry, we can collect you from near the terminal.
Weekend evenings in summer are busy, so lock in your return trip early.
about: Hotel Sorrento is a long-standing limestone hotel on Hotham Road, overlooking Port Phillip just above the Sorrento foreshore. It combines a pub and dining room with accommodation, and it is a favourite for long lunches, birthdays and summer evenings watching the bay.

We take locals and visitors to the hotel from across the southern peninsula, from Rye and Blairgowrie to Portsea, and bring them home at closing time. Guests staying overnight book us for Melbourne Airport transfers, rides to the back beaches and trips to wineries further inland. We also handle pick-ups for people arriving on the Queenscliff ferry. In the cooler months the hotel is quieter, and locals from Sorrento and Portsea book us for a weekend meal or a midweek catch-up. The southern end of the peninsula has fewer taxis than the city, so a set pick-up time is the surest way to get home when you want to.

For travellers who use a wheelchair, our ramp-equipped van and Maxi WAT both have four-point restraints and air-conditioning, and our drivers help door to door. Groups of up to eight can share the Maxi WAT. MPTP cards are accepted for eligible passengers.

faq.q: Is it easy to get a taxi from Hotel Sorrento late at night?
faq.a: Sorrento gets very busy in summer, so it is best to book your return ahead rather than hoping for a car on the spot. We operate 24 hours, and a booking made in advance means a vehicle is set aside for your time. Booking online takes about two minutes.

faq.q: Can a wheelchair user get to Hotel Sorrento by taxi?
faq.a: Yes. Book our wheelchair accessible van or Maxi WAT and the driver will help you from your door to the hotel entrance. Hotham Road slopes, so we can drop you as close to the entrance as the kerb allows. It is worth checking with the hotel about step-free access inside.

name: Portsea Hotel
description: Taxi to the Portsea Hotel for summer afternoons on the lawn, dinners and stays. Return trips on the southern peninsula, including wheelchair taxis.
entrance: We drop you at the front of the hotel on Point Nepean Road, opposite the Portsea foreshore and pier.
spot: Pick-ups are from outside the hotel on Point Nepean Road. On peak days we may stop a little along the road if traffic is heavy, and we will tell you where.
parking: Summer weekends at Portsea mean full car parks and lots of drinking on the lawn, so a taxi is the sensible way home.
access: Let us know if anyone needs the wheelchair van or a hand getting from the kerb to the entrance.
tips: Summer weekends are the busiest time at Portsea, so book your return pick-up before you arrive.
Combine your visit with a walk at nearby Point Nepean National Park.
If your group is splitting up at the end of the day, book separate cars for different destinations.
about: The Portsea Hotel is a historic pub on Point Nepean Road with a big lawn running down towards the bay. It is famous on the peninsula for summer afternoons, and it also offers dining and accommodation. Being near the very end of the peninsula, it draws crowds from Sorrento, Rye and well beyond.

Our taxis are a common sight outside on warm weekends. We run groups from holiday houses in Blairgowrie, Rye and Rosebud, bring them home once the sun goes down, and take overnight guests to and from Melbourne Airport. It is also a handy stop after a day at Point Nepean National Park. Visitors crossing on the ferry from Queenscliff to Sorrento can also book us for the short run on to Portsea.

We have sedans for couples and small groups, plus a wheelchair accessible van and a Maxi WAT for passengers who use wheelchairs or need extra room. The Maxi WAT seats six plus two wheelchairs, which suits family gatherings. On the busiest summer days, demand is high right along the southern peninsula, so booking ahead matters.

faq.q: How do we get home from the Portsea Hotel on a busy summer day?
faq.a: Book your return before you arrive. On hot weekends many people want to leave at the same time, and a booked car is held for your time. Tell us the number of passengers and destinations, and we can send one larger vehicle or several sedans depending on where everyone is going.

faq.q: Can you pick us up from Point Nepean and take us to the Portsea Hotel?
faq.a: Yes. Let us know where in the park you will finish, ideally the main entrance area or a car park private vehicles can reach, and the time you expect to be there. It is a short run to the hotel, and we can book your trip home from the pub at the same time.

name: Royal Hotel Mornington
description: Taxi to the Royal Hotel Mornington on the Esplanade for meals, events and overnight stays. Sedans and wheelchair accessible taxis, 24 hours.
entrance: We drop you at the front of the hotel on the Esplanade, near the top of Main Street.
spot: Pick-ups are from the Esplanade outside the hotel. On busy evenings or market days we may stop just along the street, and we will let you know where.
parking: Main Street and the Esplanade are packed on weekends, and a taxi to the Royal saves both the parking hunt and the drive home after drinks.
access: Tell us if you need the wheelchair van; the driver can help you from the kerb to the door.
tips: Combine dinner with a walk down to Mornington harbour and Mothers Beach.
On Wednesday market days Main Street is busy, so allow extra time.
Book return trips ahead for birthday dinners and functions, especially on Friday and Saturday nights.
about: The Royal Hotel is one of Mornington’s historic hotels, standing on the Esplanade at the top of Main Street with views over the harbour and Port Phillip. It is a popular spot for celebrations, Friday drinks and long weekend lunches.

We bring diners in from Mount Martha, Mornington, Frankston and the hinterland and take them home when they are done, which means nobody in the group has to stay on lemonade. Visitors staying in the hotel book us for transfers to and from Melbourne Airport and Frankston station, and for day trips to wineries and the hot springs. Market days and summer weekends bring heavy traffic to the top of Main Street, and a taxi to the door means you arrive in time for your booking without circling for a park.

Our wheelchair accessible van and Maxi WAT carry passengers in their own chairs with four-point restraints, and carers travel along with them. MPTP cards and NDIS accounts are accepted. For larger family groups, the Maxi WAT seats up to eight. Friday and Saturday nights are our busiest times in Mornington.

faq.q: Can you collect us from Frankston station and take us to the Royal Hotel?
faq.a: Yes. Book a pick-up at Frankston station with your expected arrival time and we will bring you to the Esplanade outside the hotel. It is a straightforward trip along the coast. If you are staying overnight, you can book your return to the station or the airport at the same time.

faq.q: Is the Royal Hotel close to Mornington harbour?
faq.a: Yes, it sits on the Esplanade above the harbour, so it is a short walk down to the pier and Mothers Beach. If anyone in your group would rather not walk, we can drop you closer to the water and pick you up from the hotel afterwards.

name: Mornington Hotel
description: Taxi to the Mornington Hotel on Main Street for pub nights, footy and parties. Book a sedan or wheelchair taxi home and skip the drive.
entrance: We drop you outside the pub on Main Street in the centre of Mornington.
spot: Pick-ups are on Main Street outside the hotel. If the kerb is blocked we will stop as close as we safely can and let you know by phone.
parking: A big night at a pub is exactly when you should not be driving, and Main Street parking is scarce on weekends anyway.
access: Let us know if you need the wheelchair van or help getting in and out; our drivers assist door to door.
tips: Book a set pick-up time for late nights; Main Street gets busy around closing.
For birthday groups, the Maxi WAT can take up to eight seated passengers together.
If you are heading to another venue afterwards, tell us when you book so we can plan the route.
about: The Mornington Hotel is a well-known pub on Main Street, in the heart of Mornington’s shopping and dining strip. It is a regular spot for meals, drinks, live sport and birthday gatherings, and it draws locals from right across the northern peninsula.

Our taxis do plenty of pub runs here. Groups book us from Mount Martha, Mornington, Moorooduc and Frankston so that nobody needs to be the designated driver, and we bring everyone home afterwards. Weekend evenings and big sporting nights are the busiest times, and booking a return trip in advance means you are not left waiting on the footpath. We also handle early-evening drop-offs for work functions and farewells, then a second run later once the celebrations wind down. If your group is moving on to a restaurant or another venue in Mornington, mention it when you book and we can plan both legs.

Passengers who use wheelchairs are welcome. Our accessible van carries one wheelchair plus four seated passengers, and the Maxi WAT carries two wheelchairs plus six seated, with a hydraulic hoist for heavier power chairs. MPTP cards are accepted for eligible passengers, and carers ride along.

faq.q: Can we book a taxi home from the Mornington Hotel in advance?
faq.a: Yes, and we recommend it, especially for Friday and Saturday nights. Book online in about two minutes or call us, choose your pick-up time, and you will receive confirmation by SMS or email. If you are running late, call and we will do our best to adjust the time.

faq.q: Can a group of friends travel together from the pub?
faq.a: For groups of up to four, a sedan is usually fine. Larger groups can book the Maxi WAT, which seats up to eight when no wheelchairs are on board, or we can send two cars if people are going to different suburbs. Mention the drop-off addresses when booking.

name: Hotel Rye
description: Taxi to Hotel Rye on Point Nepean Road for meals, drinks and summer evenings by the bay. Wheelchair accessible taxis and return trips available.
entrance: We drop you outside the hotel on Point Nepean Road, across from the Rye foreshore.
spot: Pick-up is on Point Nepean Road in front of the hotel. In peak summer traffic we may stop just along the road, and we will let you know where.
parking: Rye’s foreshore is crowded with campers and day-trippers in summer, so a taxi saves the parking hassle and keeps drink-driving off the table.
access: Tell us when booking if anyone needs the wheelchair van or help crossing from the kerb to the entrance.
tips: Summer and school holidays bring heavy traffic along Point Nepean Road, so book return trips early.
Make an evening of it with a walk on Rye pier before dinner.
Staying at the foreshore campground? We can pick you up from the entrance nearest your site.
about: Hotel Rye is a pub and dining venue on Point Nepean Road, facing the foreshore and the long Rye pier. It is a gathering place for locals year-round and fills with holidaymakers over summer, when Rye’s foreshore camping ground and beaches are packed.

We run guests here from holiday houses in Tootgarook, Blairgowrie and Rosebud, and from the camping grounds along the foreshore. After a meal and a few drinks, a booked taxi home is easier than finding the car again in the dark. We also take people on to Sorrento, Portsea or the hot springs at Fingal. Holidaymakers often ask us for a combined trip, starting at Hotel Rye for lunch and continuing to Sorrento or Portsea for the afternoon. Out of season, when Rye is calmer, locals book us for midweek dinners and catch-ups with friends.

For travellers with mobility needs, our wheelchair accessible van has a rear ramp, and the Maxi WAT has a hydraulic hoist and room for two wheelchairs plus six seated passengers. All our wheelchair vehicles have four-point restraints and air-conditioning, which helps on hot summer evenings.

faq.q: Can you pick us up from the Rye foreshore campground?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us which section of the foreshore you are staying in and the nearest entrance or landmark, and we will meet you there. It is worth booking your return from Hotel Rye at the same time, as taxis on the southern peninsula are in heavy demand over summer.

faq.q: Is there a taxi for a group going from Hotel Rye to Sorrento?
faq.a: Yes. Sedans carry up to four passengers, and the Maxi WAT seats up to eight when no wheelchairs are aboard. Let us know your group size and destination, and we will suggest the best option. Booking ahead is wise on summer evenings when Point Nepean Road is busy.

name: Woodman Estate
description: Taxi to Woodman Estate in Moorooduc for weddings, events and country stays. Book sedans, wheelchair taxis or the Maxi for guest transport.
entrance: We drive in from Graydens Road and drop you at the main reception or event area; tell us which when you book.
spot: Pick-up is at the main building or wherever the venue directs vehicles for your event. Let us know the meeting point and we will come to it.
parking: Weddings and celebrations at Woodman Estate usually run late with plenty of drinks, and a booked taxi gets guests home safely on country roads.
access: The estate has outdoor and garden areas, so let us know if anyone needs help on uneven ground, and check paths with the venue.
tips: Send us your event timings early so we can schedule guest pick-ups in waves.
Graydens Road is unlit in parts, so book returns rather than calling on the night.
Guests staying in Mornington or Frankston can share the Maxi WAT to cut down on cars.
about: Woodman Estate is a rural property in Moorooduc offering accommodation and event spaces, and it is best known as a wedding venue. Its setting among paddocks and gardens makes it popular for celebrations, but it also means it is well away from trains and buses.

We transport wedding and event guests between the estate and accommodation in Mornington, Mount Martha, Frankston and further afield. Our booking system lets you schedule several pick-ups for the end of the night, so guests are not all calling at once. We also run guests staying at the estate to Melbourne Airport and to local wineries. Couples planning a wedding can share our booking details with guests early, so people know a ride home is already arranged. That makes the evening more relaxed for everyone, including the hosts, who no longer need to worry about how guests are getting back to town.

Families with older relatives or wheelchair users often choose our Maxi WAT, which carries two wheelchairs plus six seated passengers, while the accessible van suits one chair and four others. Every wheelchair vehicle has four-point restraints and lap-sash seatbelts. Peak wedding months fill quickly, so book as early as you can.

faq.q: Can you transport wedding guests to and from Woodman Estate?
faq.a: Yes. Give us the guest numbers, pick-up addresses, any wheelchair users and the ceremony and finish times. We will suggest a mix of sedans, the accessible van and the Maxi WAT, and send confirmations by SMS or email. Booking early in wedding season is recommended.

faq.q: Is Woodman Estate easy to reach without a car?
faq.a: It is in a rural part of Moorooduc, so public transport is not practical for most guests. A taxi from Frankston station, Mornington or a nearby hotel is the simplest option. We can collect you at the time you need and bring you back after your event.

name: Quest Frankston on the Bay
description: Taxi to Quest Frankston on the Bay serviced apartments for business trips, hospital visits and airport transfers. Wheelchair taxis on request.
entrance: We drop you at the main entrance and reception of the apartment building.
spot: Pick-up is at the front of the property. Tell us your apartment block or wing if there is more than one entrance, and we will meet you there.
parking: Frankston’s central streets are busy on weekdays, and a taxi to your meeting, the hospital or the station avoids timed parking altogether.
access: Let us know if you need the wheelchair van or help with luggage; drivers assist from the door.
tips: Staying while visiting a patient? Our taxis run to Frankston Hospital and other health services around the area.
Add your flight number for airport transfers so we track your arrival.
For business trips, book your daily trips in advance to keep your schedule predictable.
about: Quest Frankston on the Bay offers serviced apartments close to the Frankston foreshore and the town centre. It is used by business travellers, families visiting relatives, and people staying near Frankston for medical appointments or hospital visits.

We see plenty of Quest guests on our daily runs. Typical trips include Melbourne Airport transfers with flight tracking, rides to Frankston station, and trips to Frankston Hospital, Monash University Peninsula campus, or business parks around Carrum Downs and Dandenong South. Guests also use us for evenings out in Mornington or wineries further down the peninsula. Longer-stay guests in Frankston for work, study or family reasons often set up regular trips, such as a daily run to a hospital or office. Ask for a fixed quote if the same journey repeats, and each booking is confirmed by SMS or email so you know a car is coming.

If you or a family member uses a wheelchair, our accessible van and Maxi WAT both have four-point restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning. We accept MPTP cards, NDIS and aged-care accounts, and carers travel with the passenger. Fixed quotes are available on request for regular trips during a longer stay.

faq.q: Can you take me from Quest Frankston on the Bay to Frankston Hospital?
faq.a: Yes. Book a pick-up time and tell us the department or entrance you need, and we will drop you as close as possible. For return trips, our pick-up when ready option lets you tap I’m ready or call us when your appointment or visit finishes.

faq.q: Do you offer airport transfers from Frankston?

about: The Flinders Hotel is the local pub in Flinders, a small seaside village on Western Port near the south-eastern corner of the peninsula. It is a hub for locals and a regular stop for visitors exploring the coastline, the pier and the nearby wine country around Main Ridge and Red Hill.

Because Flinders is relatively remote, people often book a taxi rather than taking on the drive home after a meal and a few drinks. We bring groups from Red Hill, Shoreham, Balnarring and Rosebud, and run guests on to cellar doors or back to their accommodation. Booking ahead matters here, as cars are not waiting on every corner. Walkers finishing a section of the coastal track around Flinders sometimes call in for a meal before heading home, and we can collect them from the pub at the end of the day.

Our fleet includes sedans and two wheelchair accessible vehicles: a van with a rear ramp and a Maxi WAT with a hydraulic hoist that suits heavier power chairs. Both have four-point restraints. Drivers help door to door, and Locals with an MPTP card can use it on trips to and from the pub.

faq.q: Is it hard to get a taxi in Flinders at night?
faq.a: Flinders is a small village some distance from the bigger towns, so it is best to book your trip home ahead of time rather than calling on the spot. Set a pick-up time when you book your trip in, and we will have a car committed to it. We operate 24 hours a day.

faq.q: Can you take us from the Flinders Hotel to wineries in Main Ridge?
faq.a: Yes. Main Ridge and Red Hill cellar doors are a short drive inland. Let us know which wineries you plan to visit and the order, and we can book each leg so you move between them smoothly and get back to Flinders or home at the end of the day.

about: The Dromana Hotel is a long-established pub on the Dromana foreshore, looking out across Port Phillip at the foot of Arthurs Seat. It serves meals and drinks to locals and visitors and is a popular place to watch the sun go down over the bay.

Our taxis bring diners from Safety Beach, McCrae, Rosebud and Red Hill so the whole group can relax, and we take them home afterwards. Holidaymakers staying along the foreshore use us to get to the pub, the Arthurs Seat Eagle, the wineries of Red Hill and the hot springs at Fingal. On summer evenings the foreshore is crowded with campers and day-trippers, and a set pick-up time is the easiest way home. Out of season, locals use us for midweek meals and footy nights, when the pub is quieter but the drive home still matters.

For passengers with a wheelchair, we have a ramp-equipped van and a Maxi WAT with a hydraulic hoist and space for two wheelchairs plus six seated passengers. Drivers secure each chair with four-point restraints. NDIS and aged-care accounts are welcome, and carers ride along at no extra fuss.

faq.q: Can you take us from the Dromana Hotel to Red Hill wineries?
faq.a: Yes. The Red Hill wine region is just up the hill from Dromana. Tell us which cellar doors you want to visit and roughly how long you will stay, and we can book each leg so you are collected on time. It is a good way to enjoy tastings without anyone driving.

faq.q: Do you have wheelchair taxis in the Dromana area?
faq.a: Yes. Our wheelchair accessible van and Maxi WAT both serve Dromana and the surrounding towns. Book ahead, mention the wheelchair type, and the driver will help you from your door to the hotel entrance. Eligible passengers can use their MPTP card.

about: Crown Towers is the luxury hotel at the Crown Melbourne complex on the Southbank side of the Yarra. The precinct includes restaurants, bars, a casino and event spaces, and it is close to the Melbourne Convention and Exhibition Centre and the city’s arts precinct.

Peninsula and Frankston residents often book us for a city night away, a milestone dinner or a show, avoiding the drive up the freeway and the cost of city parking. We also take hotel guests to Melbourne Airport and to the peninsula’s wineries and hot springs for day trips from the city. Some customers book us to Crown for a show or concert at one of the Southbank venues, then stay the night rather than face the late trip home. Others use the hotel as a base before an early flight. One booking can cover the trip up and the trip home a day or two later.

For guests with mobility needs, our wheelchair accessible van and Maxi WAT both travel to Melbourne. The Maxi WAT carries two wheelchairs plus six seated passengers, which suits family groups heading to a celebration. Fixed quotes are available on request for longer trips like this.

faq.q: Can you take us from Mornington to Crown Towers and back the next day?

faq.q: Do you provide wheelchair taxis into the city?
faq.a: Yes. Our accessible van and Maxi WAT travel anywhere in Melbourne, including Southbank. Tell us the type of chair you use and how many people are travelling. The driver secures the chair with four-point restraints and helps you from the vehicle to the hotel entrance.

about: Pan Pacific Melbourne is a large hotel at South Wharf, right next to the Melbourne Convention and Exhibition Centre and overlooking the Yarra. It is a natural choice for conference delegates and exhibition visitors, and it is also used for city getaways and events.

Exhibitors often arrive with display materials or extra bags, so let us know about luggage when you book and we will send a vehicle with room. For multi-day conferences, some guests stay at the hotel during the week and book us to take them home to the peninsula on the final afternoon.

Carers travel with the passenger, and NDIS and aged-care accounts are accepted. A fixed quote can be arranged for regular trips during multi-day events.

faq.q: Can you take me from Frankston to Pan Pacific Melbourne for a conference?

Peninsula residents book us for anniversary nights, functions and weekends in the city. Because the hotel is close to the MCG and Rod Laver Arena, we also drop guests here before big events so they can walk to the game or concert. Return trips to the peninsula are easy to arrange at the same time. Older relatives travelling up for a family celebration often prefer a door-to-door trip to trains and trams, and our drivers can help with bags from your front door to the hotel lobby.

Our fleet includes sedans for couples and small groups, a wheelchair accessible van with a rear ramp, and a Maxi WAT with a hydraulic hoist. Wheelchair passengers stay in their own chairs with four-point restraints, and drivers help door to door. Fixed quotes are available on request.

faq.q: Is Park Hyatt Melbourne close to the MCG?
faq.a: Yes. It is on the eastern side of the city near the Fitzroy Gardens, and the MCG and Melbourne Park are a short ride away. We can drop you at the hotel and take you to the stadium later, or collect you after the event to bring you back.

faq.q: Can you bring wedding guests from the peninsula to Park Hyatt?

faq.q: Can you take us from Frankston to Grand Hyatt Melbourne for a theatre weekend?

faq.q: Can a wheelchair user travel to the Grand Hyatt with you?
faq.a: Yes. Book our wheelchair accessible van or Maxi WAT and tell us about the chair. The driver will help you into the vehicle, secure the chair with four-point restraints, and assist you to the hotel entrance on Collins Street. Carers can travel in the same vehicle.

Southbank is handy for Crown, the Arts Centre and the riverside restaurants, so many guests book a single trip up and walk everywhere during their stay. Our wheelchair accessible van has a rear ramp and room for one wheelchair plus four seated passengers, and the Maxi WAT has a hydraulic hoist for heavier power chairs. Both have four-point restraints and air-conditioning. Carers travel with the passenger, and fixed quotes are available on request.

faq.q: Is The Langham close to Arts Centre Melbourne?
faq.a: Yes. The hotel is on the Southbank promenade, a short walk from the Arts Centre and Hamer Hall. We can drop you at the hotel before the show and collect you from the Arts Centre afterwards if you prefer. Tell us your plans when booking.

faq.q: Can I book a return trip from the peninsula to The Langham?

about: PARKROYAL Melbourne Airport is a hotel within the Melbourne Airport precinct at Tullamarine, a short walk from the terminals. Travellers use it the night before an early flight, after a late arrival, or for meetings close to the airport.

For peninsula and Frankston residents, the journey to Tullamarine is a long one, so staying overnight before a dawn departure can make the trip less stressful. We drive customers to the hotel the evening before and collect them when they land, using flight tracking so pick-ups move with delays. Families heading overseas with young children or older parents often find an overnight stay makes the trip less hectic, and our drivers help with bags from your front door to the hotel. When you come home, we can meet you at the terminal, or at the hotel if you stay a night after landing.

Travellers with mobility needs can book our wheelchair accessible van or Maxi WAT, both of which have room for luggage and four-point restraints for wheelchairs. Drivers help with bags and assist door to door. Fixed quotes are available on request for airport trips.

Most of our passengers come for a long lunch or a tasting, often as part of a day visiting several cellar doors along Red Hill Road and Shoreham Road. Taking a taxi means nobody has to count glasses or tackle the hill roads afterwards. Guests staying in the suites also book us for transfers from Melbourne Airport or Frankston station.

It is a frequent stop on wine-touring days, and the cluster of cellar doors on Shoreham Road makes it easy to add one or two more. We also carry wedding and function guests to and from events here. Locals also choose Montalto to celebrate milestones, booking a table for the family and leaving the transport to us so the guest of honour does not need to drive.

faq.q: How long should we allow at Montalto?

faq.q: Can you take a wheelchair user to Montalto?

about: Red Hill Estate is a winery on Shoreham Road in Red Hill South, set on a slope with broad views towards Western Port. Its cellar door and dining room are a popular stop for visitors to the Red Hill wine district, and it also hosts functions and celebrations.

We drop many visitors here as part of a day touring Shoreham Road’s wineries. With several cellar doors within a short drive, a taxi means you can sample freely and move between venues without anyone acting as the driver. Wedding and function guests often book us for the trip home at the end of the evening. Visitors staying in Mornington, Dromana or Rosebud often start their day here, then work their way along Shoreham Road to the neighbouring cellar doors. With a taxi, you can plan the route around your bookings rather than around who is driving, and change plans on the day by calling us.

For wheelchair users, our ramp-equipped van and hoist-equipped Maxi WAT both visit Red Hill’s wineries regularly. Every wheelchair vehicle has four-point restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning, so you stay comfortable on country roads. Book early during the busiest months of the year.

faq.q: Can you take our group from Red Hill Estate to other wineries?

faq.q: Is Red Hill Estate a good venue for a function, and can you transport guests?

Friends celebrating birthdays and couples on weekends away make up much of our trade here. Because the Shoreham Road wineries sit so close together, a taxi day here does not need to be long. Some groups visit just two venues, tasting at one and lunching at the other, then head home by mid-afternoon. Others make a full day of it, and we fit around either plan.

about: Ten Minutes by Tractor is a Main Ridge winery and restaurant on Mornington-Flinders Road. The name refers to its vineyards, which sit a short tractor ride apart. It is well known for its pinot noir and chardonnay and for its fine-dining restaurant, which draws visitors from across Melbourne.

Diners often book us for the trip up and back so the whole party can enjoy a degustation and wine pairings without a designated driver. Main Ridge is high in the peninsula’s hinterland, and the roads home are winding and dark at night, so a taxi is the comfortable choice. We also carry guests from Sorrento, Mornington and Frankston for special occasions. It is also a popular choice for anniversaries and engagement dinners, and couples often ask us to collect them from accommodation in Sorrento, Red Hill or Flinders so the evening runs smoothly.

For passengers using wheelchairs, the accessible van carries one wheelchair and four seated passengers, and the Maxi WAT takes two wheelchairs and six seated. Drivers help from door to door. Weekend lunches and dinners book out, so reserve your taxi when you make your restaurant booking.

faq.q: How do we get home from a dinner at Ten Minutes by Tractor?
faq.a: Book your return trip when you book your drop-off, choosing a time a little after your meal is expected to end. If the evening runs long, call us to adjust. We operate 24 hours, but booking ahead guarantees a car in the hinterland late at night.

faq.q: Can you bring guests from Melbourne to Ten Minutes by Tractor?
faq.a: Yes. We travel anywhere in Melbourne, and can collect you from home or a hotel and bring you to Main Ridge. The fare estimate is shown on the booking form, and you can ask for a fixed quote for a long return trip.

about: Pt. Leo Estate sits on Frankston-Flinders Road at Merricks, overlooking Western Port. It combines a vineyard and cellar door with restaurants, a wine terrace and a large sculpture park featuring works by Australian and international artists set across lawns that run towards the coast.

It is a popular destination for long lunches, birthdays and day trips. People book a taxi so they can enjoy a glass on the terrace and wander the sculptures without anyone driving home. We bring visitors from Mornington, Frankston and further afield, and pick up guests from functions and celebrations held at the estate. Its position on the eastern side of the peninsula also makes it an easy stop for visitors from Hastings, Somers and Balnarring. If your group is staying in different towns, we can collect people from several addresses, bring everyone to the estate together, then reverse the route at the end.

Our wheelchair accessible van and Maxi WAT both visit Pt. Leo regularly. The Maxi WAT seats up to six plus two wheelchairs, ideal for families travelling together. All our accessible vehicles have four-point restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning, and carers travel with the passenger.

faq.q: Is there much to do at Pt. Leo Estate apart from eating and drinking?
faq.a: Yes. The estate has a large sculpture park that you can walk around, with artworks spread over lawns overlooking Western Port. Allow extra time to explore before or after your meal, and choose a return pick-up time that gives you room to enjoy it.

faq.q: Can you take us from Pt. Leo Estate to another winery?
faq.a: Yes. Stonier and Merricks Estate are close by, and Red Hill’s cellar doors are a short drive inland. Tell us your planned stops when booking, and we will arrange each leg so you can move between them easily. Confirm any lunch booking times first.

about: Paringa Estate is a family-run winery on Paringa Road in Red Hill South, known for its pinot noir, chardonnay and shiraz. It has a cellar door and a restaurant that looks over the vineyard, and it is a regular stop for visitors exploring the wineries around Red Hill.

Our customers often visit Paringa as one stop on a wine-tasting day, or book a long lunch and let us handle the journey there and back. Because so many cellar doors sit close together in this part of the peninsula, it is easy to plan a day that takes in two or three without the need for a driver. Wine enthusiasts who come specifically for Paringa’s reds often plan a slower visit, with a tasting followed by a meal, so it pays to set a generous return time or call us when you are ready.

Sedans suit couples and small groups, while the Maxi WAT seats up to eight. For passengers who use wheelchairs, the accessible van has a rear ramp and the Maxi WAT has a hydraulic hoist. All our accessible vehicles carry four-point restraints, and drivers assist door to door.

faq.q: Can you take us to Paringa Estate and two other wineries in one day?
faq.a: Yes. Red Hill South has several cellar doors close together, including Port Phillip Estate, Montalto and Red Hill Estate. Tell us your order and timings, and we will book each trip so you are collected and moved on without waiting.

faq.q: Do you offer wheelchair taxis to Paringa Estate?
faq.a: Yes. Book the wheelchair accessible van or Maxi WAT and tell us about the chair. The driver will help you from your door to the entrance, and it is worth asking the estate about accessible seating and routes inside. A carer is welcome to ride along.

about: Crittenden Estate is a family winery on Harrisons Road in the Dromana hinterland, run by the Crittenden family. It produces a range of cool-climate wines alongside Italian and Spanish varieties, and its cellar door and dining area sit beside a lake surrounded by vines.

Visitors book us to reach Crittenden for tastings, lunches and private events. Because it is a short drive from both Dromana and Red Hill, it is easy to include in a wider wine-touring day. Guests staying in Safety Beach, Mount Martha and Mornington often use us for the return trip so they can relax and enjoy the wines. The range runs from familiar pinot noir and chardonnay to less common European grapes, which makes it a good stop for curious tasters. With so many styles on offer, a taxi means nobody has to sit the tasting out, and we can continue on to Red Hill or Moorooduc afterwards.

For passengers with a wheelchair, our accessible van carries one chair plus four seated passengers, and the Maxi WAT carries two chairs plus six. Chairs are held with four-point restraints, and every passenger has a lap-sash seatbelt. NDIS participants and MPTP cardholders can book these trips in the usual way.

faq.q: Is Crittenden Estate close to Dromana?
faq.a: Yes. It sits in the hills just behind Dromana, a short drive from the foreshore and the Nepean Highway. We can bring you from anywhere on the peninsula and collect you at a time you choose, or you can call us when you are ready to leave.

faq.q: Can you take guests to an event at Crittenden Estate?
faq.a: Yes. Let us know the event times, how many guests and where they are coming from. We will suggest a mix of sedans, the wheelchair van and the Maxi WAT, and confirm each booking by SMS or email. Booking early helps during busy months.

about: Foxeys Hangout is a family-run winery on White Hill Road in Red Hill, known for its sparkling wines and its relaxed cellar door, where visitors can taste and share plates of food made in its kitchen. It has a friendly, informal feel and is a favourite with groups of friends.

We take many groups to Foxeys for birthdays and weekends away. Booking a taxi means everyone can enjoy the tasting and the bubbles, and nobody has to navigate Red Hill’s winding roads afterwards. We also offer trips on to other cellar doors in Red Hill and Merricks North. Foxeys also works well as the last stop of a day, with relaxed seating and food to share. If you start in Mornington or Mount Martha, we can take you to two or three Red Hill cellar doors first and finish here before driving everyone home.

For wheelchair users, our accessible van has a rear ramp, and the Maxi WAT has a hydraulic hoist for heavier power chairs. Both are fitted with four-point restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning. Booking ahead is wise on spring and summer weekends.

faq.q: Is Foxeys Hangout good for a group visit?
faq.a: Many groups visit for a relaxed afternoon of tasting and shared food. Book your table with the winery, then book our Maxi WAT, which seats up to eight, or several sedans. Set a return time so we are there when you finish.

faq.q: Can you take us from Foxeys Hangout to other wineries nearby?
faq.a: Yes. There are several cellar doors in Red Hill and Merricks North a short drive away. Tell us where you want to go next and when, and we will book the trip so you can move between wineries easily. Booking ahead is wise on weekends.

about: Polperro is a winery on Red Hill Road with a cellar door, a bistro and vineyard accommodation. It produces wines from its own vineyards around Red Hill, and its relaxed dining room makes it a popular place for long weekend lunches.

We drive guests to Polperro for lunch, tastings and overnight stays. Since Red Hill Road is lined with other cellar doors, it is easy to visit two or three in a day while we take care of the driving. Guests staying in the villas often book us for transfers from Melbourne Airport or Frankston station. The villas suit couples on a weekend escape, and many guests ask us to collect them from Frankston station or the airport on arrival. Others come only for lunch and leave the car at home, which makes the bistro’s wine list much easier to enjoy.

Our sedans carry up to four passengers, and the Maxi WAT seats up to eight or carries two wheelchairs plus six passengers. All our wheelchair vehicles have four-point restraints and lap-sash seatbelts, and drivers help from the car to the door. MPTP cardholders are welcome on any of these trips.

faq.q: Can you take us to Polperro and pick us up after lunch?
faq.a: Yes. Book your drop-off and return trip together, choosing a return time after your expected finish. If you decide to stay longer, call us and we will adjust where we can. Confirmations are sent by SMS or email. Booking ahead is recommended on weekends.

faq.q: We are staying at Polperro. Can you take us to other wineries?
faq.a: Yes. Many cellar doors are a short drive away along Red Hill Road and Shoreham Road. Let us know your plans for the day, and we can book each trip so you can enjoy the wine without anyone driving. Many are within a short drive.

about: Main Ridge Estate is one of the pioneering vineyards of the Mornington Peninsula, planted in the 1970s in the cool, elevated country around Main Ridge and Red Hill. It is known for its pinot noir and chardonnay and has a small cellar door where visitors can taste the wines.

Wine lovers come here to taste at the source, often combining a visit with lunch at a nearby restaurant. A taxi means nobody has to drive the narrow, winding roads around Main Ridge after tasting. We can bring you from anywhere on the peninsula and collect you at the end of the visit. Because the cellar door is small and focused on tasting, many visitors build a short tour around it, adding lunch at a nearby restaurant or a stop at another Main Ridge winery. We can collect you from accommodation in Red Hill, Sorrento or Rosebud and book each leg at once.

For passengers using wheelchairs, the accessible van and Maxi WAT have four-point restraints and lap-sash seatbelts. Drivers help you from the car to the cellar door and back. Bookings are recommended, especially for weekend trips into the hinterland.

faq.q: Is Main Ridge Estate open every day?

faq.q: Can you combine Main Ridge Estate with lunch at another winery?
faq.a: Yes. Ten Minutes by Tractor and other Main Ridge and Red Hill wineries are close by. Tell us your plans and we will book each leg of the day so you can taste and dine without anyone needing to drive.

about: Stonier is one of the established names of the Mornington Peninsula wine region, based at Merricks in the gentler country towards Western Port. It is known for chardonnay and pinot noir, and its cellar door gives visitors a chance to taste across the range.

Wine lovers book us to visit Stonier as part of a Merricks and Red Hill tour, often combining it with Pt. Leo Estate for lunch. The Merricks area is rural and spread out, so a taxi saves your group from choosing a sober driver and finding the way between wineries. Wine clubs and work groups sometimes plan a tasting at Stonier as part of a day out on the eastern side of the peninsula. If your group is coming from the city, we can collect you from home or a hotel and arrange the trip back, so nobody needs to drive after a day of tastings.

For passengers using wheelchairs, the accessible van carries one chair and four seated passengers, while the Maxi WAT carries two chairs and six seated. Drivers help from your door to the cellar door, and carers travel along. NDIS and aged-care accounts are accepted.

faq.q: Is Stonier close to Pt. Leo Estate?
faq.a: Yes. Both are in Merricks, a short drive apart, and many people visit them on the same day. Tell us the order you want to visit, along with any lunch booking, and we will arrange each leg so you are collected on time.

faq.q: Do I need to check Stonier’s opening hours before booking?
faq.a: Yes, please check directly with the winery, as cellar door hours can change and we do not keep track of them. Once you know when it is open, book your drop-off and return with us to fit. A set return time works best in rural Merricks.

about: Willow Creek Vineyard sits on Balnarring Road at Merricks North, sharing its property with Jackalope Hotel. It has a cellar door and a restaurant, and is a popular place for a long, relaxed lunch among the vines.

We take visitors to Willow Creek for tastings, lunches and celebrations, and pick them up again when they are ready. Hotel guests at Jackalope also walk over for a tasting, and we can run them to other cellar doors in Red Hill or Merricks afterwards. Balnarring Road is rural, so a booked taxi is the easiest way to get home. Many visitors come for a long weekend lunch, sharing a bottle and taking in the view across the vines. With a booked taxi, you can stay as long as you like and head home when you are ready. We also collect guests staying in Mornington, Mount Martha or Flinders.

Groups of up to eight can travel together in the Maxi WAT. For passengers who use wheelchairs, our accessible van and Maxi WAT both have four-point restraints, and drivers assist from door to door. MPTP cards and NDIS accounts can be used for vineyard outings too.

faq.q: Is Willow Creek Vineyard the same place as Jackalope Hotel?
faq.a: They share the same property on Balnarring Road at Merricks North. Willow Creek is the vineyard, cellar door and restaurant, while Jackalope is the hotel. Tell us which part of the property you are visiting so we drop you at the right building.

faq.q: Can you take us to Willow Creek for lunch and then to another winery?

about: Merricks Estate is a family-owned winery in Merricks, among the vineyards that run down towards Western Port. It is a smaller producer with a cellar door where visitors can taste the estate’s wines in a quiet country setting.

People book us to visit Merricks Estate as part of a tour of the quieter eastern side of the peninsula, often alongside Stonier and Pt. Leo Estate. Because the area is rural and roads between wineries are long and winding, a taxi lets everyone taste without having to drive. The wineries around Merricks are fewer and further apart than in Red Hill, so planning the route matters. Tell us which cellar doors you want to visit, check their opening days, and we will build the day around them. A smaller winery often means an unhurried tasting and time to talk about the wines.

Our sedans suit couples and small groups, and the Maxi WAT seats up to eight. Passengers in wheelchairs can travel in our accessible van or Maxi WAT, which are fitted with four-point restraints and air-conditioning. Drivers help you from the car to the cellar door.

faq.q: Is Merricks Estate open every day?
faq.a: Smaller wineries often open on limited days, and we do not keep track of cellar door hours. Please check with Merricks Estate directly before booking your taxi, then choose drop-off and pick-up times that fit. If you plan to visit several wineries, check each one’s hours so the day fits together.

faq.q: Can you take us to Merricks Estate and Stonier on the same day?
faq.a: Yes. Both are in Merricks, so the trip between them is short. Let us know your plans, and we will book each leg so you can move easily between cellar doors. If you would like to add Pt. Leo Estate for lunch, we can include that leg too, and collect you at the end of the day.

about: Quealy Winemakers is a family winery in Balnarring founded by winemaker Kathleen Quealy and Kevin McCarthy, known on the peninsula for pinot grigio, friulano and textural, skin-contact styles. Its cellar door offers a relaxed setting for trying wines a little different from the usual peninsula pinot and chardonnay.

Visitors book us to reach Quealy as part of a tasting day in Balnarring, Merricks North and Red Hill. With plenty to taste, a taxi is the simple way to make sure no one has to stay sober. We bring guests from Mornington, Hastings and Frankston and collect them at the end of their visit. Wine lovers interested in alternative varieties often seek out Quealy specifically, sometimes travelling from Melbourne for the day. We can collect you from home or Frankston station, take you to Balnarring and other nearby cellar doors, then bring you home in the evening.

For passengers who use wheelchairs, our accessible van has a rear ramp, and the Maxi WAT has a hydraulic hoist and space for two wheelchairs plus six seated passengers. Each chair is secured with four-point restraints for the country roads. Eligible passengers may use an MPTP card or NDIS account for the trip.

faq.q: What kind of wines does Quealy make?
faq.a: Quealy is known for pinot grigio, friulano and skin-contact or textural styles, as well as more familiar peninsula varieties. Check with the winery about current tastings and opening days, then book your taxi to fit, with a return pick-up when you are ready.

faq.q: Can you take us from Quealy to nearby wineries?

about: Yabby Lake Vineyard is a winery on Tuerong Road at Tuerong, in the northern part of the peninsula’s wine country. It is known for its pinot noir, chardonnay and syrah, and its cellar door and restaurant look out across the vines and the lake that gives it its name.

It is a short drive from Mornington and Mount Martha, so locals book us for lunches, birthdays and tastings. Visitors staying in Frankston or Melbourne often combine Yabby Lake with Moorooduc Estate or Crittenden Estate on a day that stays north of the hinterland. Its position on the northern side of the wine region makes it a natural first stop for visitors coming down from Melbourne. If you are staying in the city or in Frankston, we can collect you in the morning, take you to two or three cellar doors, and bring you home after lunch.

Our wheelchair accessible van carries one chair and four seated passengers, while the Maxi WAT carries two chairs and six seated. All wheelchair vehicles have four-point restraints and lap-sash seatbelts, and drivers help from door to door. Book ahead for spring and summer weekends.

faq.q: Is Yabby Lake Vineyard far from Mornington?
faq.a: It is in Tuerong, a short drive inland from Mornington and Mount Martha. We can collect you from home, a hotel or Frankston station and bring you to the cellar door, then take you home at the time you choose.

faq.q: Can you take a group of friends to Yabby Lake for lunch?

Because it is so close to Mornington and Frankston, it is a short taxi trip for a tasting or a weekend lunch. Visitors from Melbourne often start their wine day here before heading south, and we can help with each leg of the trip. Being so close to town, it is an easy option when you only have an afternoon free. Locals from Mount Martha and Mornington book a quick tasting before dinner, and visitors arriving at Frankston station can be at the cellar door soon after stepping off the train. Check the winery’s opening days before you book.

A sedan works well for two to four people, while the Maxi WAT takes groups of up to eight. For passengers who use wheelchairs, the accessible van and Maxi WAT have four-point restraints and air-conditioning. MPTP cards, NDIS and aged-care accounts are accepted, and carers travel with the passenger.

faq.q: Is Moorooduc Estate close to Frankston?
faq.a: Yes. It is one of the nearest cellar doors to Frankston and Mornington, so it is a short taxi trip. We can collect you from home or Frankston station and bring you back after your tasting or lunch. Check the cellar door’s opening days first.

faq.q: Can you take us from Moorooduc Estate further down the peninsula?
