access: Let us know if you need the wheelchair van or help from the car.
tips: Book your return trip before you arrive on Friday and Saturday nights.
A crew of up to eight fits in the Maxi WAT.
Combine with dinner in Mornington’s Main Street.
about: Mornington Peninsula Brewery is a craft brewery in Mornington, brewing its beers on site and pouring them in its own bar. It is a popular place for after-work drinks, birthday gatherings and casual weekend sessions.

We bring groups here from Mount Martha, Mornington, Frankston and the hinterland, so that nobody has to drive after tasting the beers. It is also a common stop at the start or end of a night out in Mornington, with Main Street’s restaurants and pubs a short ride away. Brewery visits often run longer than planned, especially with a group trying different beers. Setting a pick-up time when you book means a ride is waiting without anyone needing to remember to call. For birthdays and work drinks, the Maxi WAT keeps everyone together, and we can drop you on Main Street for dinner afterwards.

Passengers who use wheelchairs can book our accessible van or Maxi WAT, which have four-point restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning. Drivers help door to door, and carers ride along. Weekend evenings are our busiest time, so book your return early.

faq.q: Can we book a taxi home from Mornington Peninsula Brewery?
faq.a: Yes. Book online or by phone with your pick-up time, and you will receive confirmation by SMS or email. If you are running late, call us to adjust. Booking ahead is recommended on Friday and Saturday nights. Groups can share the Maxi WAT.

faq.q: Can you take a group to the brewery and on to Main Street?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us your plans, including your group size and the next venue. For bigger crews we can send the Maxi WAT or a couple of sedans. We can book each leg of your night so you are not left waiting.

name: Peninsula Hot Springs
description: Taxi to Peninsula Hot Springs in Fingal for bathing, spa treatments and birthday groups. Book return trips, wheelchair taxis or the Maxi.
entrance: We drop you at the main arrival and reception area, where you check in for bathing or spa sessions.
spot: Drop-off and pick-up are at the main entrance drop-off area. Tell us if you are booked into the spa or another part of the site so we can meet you at the most convenient point.
parking: Car parks fill on busy weekends and holidays, and a taxi lets you leave relaxed rather than face a drive after hours in hot water.
access: Ask the springs about accessible bathing areas and paths, and let us know if you need the wheelchair van or help from the car.
tips: Book your bathing session first, then match your taxi times to it.
Allow a buffer after bathing before your pick-up so you have time to shower and change.
Weekends and school holidays are busy, so book your taxi early.
about: Peninsula Hot Springs in Fingal is a large bathing and spa venue fed by natural geothermal mineral waters. Visitors move between pools of different temperatures, including a hilltop pool with views over the peninsula, and many book spa treatments as part of their day.

We take guests here from across Melbourne and the peninsula, often for birthdays, hens days and relaxing days off. A taxi means you can arrive without the drive and leave feeling rested rather than fighting traffic. Guests staying at nearby resorts like Peppers Moonah Links or RACV Cape Schanck use us for the short hop across. Some visitors book an early session and arrive as the pools open, while others prefer the late afternoon and evening. Whatever time you choose, we can collect you from your accommodation and return you when you finish, so you do not need to drive after a long, warm soak.

For groups, the Maxi WAT seats up to eight, and for guests with mobility needs, our accessible van and Maxi WAT both have four-point restraints and air-conditioning. Drivers help from door to door, and carers travel with the passenger.

faq.q: How long should we book at Peninsula Hot Springs before our return taxi?
faq.a: That depends on your bathing session and any treatments. Allow time to shower and change after bathing, and add a buffer before your pick-up time. If you are not sure, choose a later time or call us when ready, though a set time is more reliable on busy days.

faq.q: Can you bring a group from Melbourne to the hot springs?
faq.a: Yes. We travel anywhere in Melbourne. The Maxi WAT seats up to eight, or we can send several sedans. Book drop-off and return times together, and you can ask for a fixed quote for a longer trip like this. Mention any wheelchair users too.

name: Alba Thermal Springs and Spa
description: Taxi to Alba Thermal Springs and Spa in Fingal for thermal bathing, spa days and dining. Book a sedan, Maxi or wheelchair accessible taxi.
entrance: We drop you at the main entrance and reception, where you check in for your session.
spot: Drop-off and pick-up are at the front entrance. Let us know if you are dining at the restaurant only so we know where to meet you.
parking: After a long soak and perhaps a glass of wine with lunch, a taxi is the more relaxed way home.
access: Ask the venue about accessible pools and paths, and let us know if you need the wheelchair van or help from the car.
tips: Pre-book your bathing session, then match your taxi times to it.
Allow time to change and relax before your pick-up.
Alba is close to Peninsula Hot Springs and Peppers Moonah Links, so it suits guests staying nearby.
about: Alba Thermal Springs and Spa opened in Fingal in 2023, offering thermal mineral pools set among landscaped gardens, along with spa treatments and dining. It has quickly become a popular choice for relaxing days out on the southern peninsula.

Visitors book us to make a day at Alba stress free, often as a birthday treat or a getaway with friends. Without needing to drive, you can enjoy a full session, lunch and a drink, then head home relaxed. Guests staying in Rye, Sorrento and Cape Schanck use us for the short trip across. With a restaurant on site, many visitors plan a long day of bathing and a meal, perhaps with a glass of wine at lunch, which is another reason to leave the car at home. If you are not sure when you will finish, choose a later pick-up or call us when you are ready.

Our sedans suit couples, and groups of up to eight can share the Maxi WAT. Wheelchair passengers can travel in the accessible van or Maxi WAT, with four-point restraints and lap-sash seatbelts. Weekends and holidays are popular, so book early.

faq.q: Is Alba Thermal Springs near Peninsula Hot Springs?
faq.a: Yes. Both are in Fingal, a short drive apart. Make sure to tell us which venue you are visiting when you book, so we drop you at the right place. We can also take you to nearby resorts or wineries afterwards.

faq.q: Can you take a wheelchair user to Alba Thermal Springs?
faq.a: Yes. Book our accessible van or Maxi WAT and tell us about the chair. The driver will help you from your door to the entrance. Ask Alba directly about accessible pools and change areas before your visit. Carers travel with the passenger at no extra fuss.

name: Arthurs Seat Eagle
description: Taxi to the Arthurs Seat Eagle gondola for bay views from the summit. Drop-off at the base or summit station, with wheelchair taxis available.
entrance: We can drop you at the base station in Dromana or the summit station at Arthurs Seat; tell us which when booking.
spot: Pick-up can be at either station. If you ride one way only, let us know which station you will finish at.
parking: On clear weekends both stations can be busy, and a taxi makes a one-way ride easy without needing to return for the car.
access: Ask the Eagle about accessible gondolas and paths, and let us know if you need the wheelchair van or help from the car.
tips: Ride one way and let us pick you up at the other station.
Combine with the Enchanted Adventure Garden nearby.
Choose a clear day for the best views across Port Phillip.
about: The Arthurs Seat Eagle is a gondola running between a base station in Dromana and a summit station at Arthurs Seat. The ride offers broad views across Port Phillip, and it is one of the peninsula’s most popular attractions for families and visitors.

A taxi suits the Eagle well because you can ride one way and be met at the other station. Many families book us to drop them at the base, then collect them at the summit after a walk or a visit to the Enchanted Adventure Garden nearby. We also bring visitors from Rosebud, Sorrento and Mornington who prefer not to drive up the mountain road. Visitors from Melbourne often make a day of it, riding the Eagle, exploring the summit and then heading down to Dromana or Red Hill for lunch. We can book each part of the day in one go, so you are not left waiting at the top of the mountain.

Our wheelchair accessible van and Maxi WAT have four-point restraints and air-conditioning, and our drivers help from door to door. The Maxi WAT seats up to six plus two wheelchairs, suiting families and small groups.

faq.q: Can you drop us at the base station and pick us up at the summit?
faq.a: Yes, that is a popular option. Book the drop-off at the base station and a pick-up at the summit station at a time that allows for the ride and any time at the top. If you are unsure, call us when ready.

faq.q: Is the Arthurs Seat Eagle close to other attractions?
faq.a: Yes. The Enchanted Adventure Garden is nearby on Arthurs Seat, and the Dromana foreshore is close to the base station. Tell us your plans, and we can book each leg so you can move between them without the car. Families often do the garden in the morning.

name: Ashcombe Maze & Lavender Gardens
description: Taxi to Ashcombe Maze & Lavender Gardens in Shoreham for hedge mazes and gardens. Book family groups, return trips and wheelchair taxis.
entrance: We drop you at the main entrance near the visitor area and café.
spot: We set down and collect at the visitor entrance. If the driveway is busy on peak days, we will stop as close as safely possible.
parking: School holidays and weekends are busy, and a taxi frees parents and grandparents from the drive.
access: Garden paths include grass and gravel, so ask the venue about accessible routes, and let us know if you need help from the car.
tips: Lavender is at its best in summer, so book early during peak season.
Combine with nearby Red Hill wineries for adults in the group.
Allow plenty of time to explore the mazes and gardens.
about: Ashcombe Maze & Lavender Gardens is a family attraction on Shoreham Road, known for its tall hedge maze, lavender fields and themed gardens. There is also a café, making it an easy half-day outing for families and garden lovers.

Grandparents and families book us to reach Ashcombe without the drive, especially during school holidays. It sits near Red Hill’s wineries, so some visitors combine the maze with a tasting, leaving the driving to us. We also take groups from aged-care facilities and community organisations. Summer is popular with garden lovers and photographers who time their visit for the lavender. If your group includes people who walk slowly, plan extra time for the paths through the gardens and maze. Our drivers are happy to help with walkers, prams and bags at the start and end of your visit.

For visitors using wheelchairs, our ramp-equipped van carries one chair and four seated passengers, and the Maxi WAT carries two chairs and six seated with a hydraulic hoist. Aged-care and NDIS accounts are welcome for group outings, MPTP cards are accepted, and carers ride along.

faq.q: Is Ashcombe Maze suitable for wheelchair users?
faq.a: Some areas have grass and gravel paths, so ask the venue about accessible routes before your visit. We can bring you in our wheelchair accessible van or Maxi WAT, and the driver will help you from the car to the entrance.

faq.q: Can you take a family group to Ashcombe Maze?
faq.a: Yes. Our Maxi WAT seats up to eight, or we can send several sedans. Book drop-off and return times together, and let us know about prams or mobility aids so we send a vehicle with enough room. Weekends and school holidays are busiest.

name: Enchanted Adventure Garden
description: Taxi to the Enchanted Adventure Garden at Arthurs Seat for tree surfing, mazes and tube slides. Family return trips and wheelchair taxis.
entrance: We drop you at the main entrance near the ticket office.
spot: Drop-off and pick-up are at the front entrance on Purves Road. On busy days we will stop as close as safely possible.
parking: Peak school-holiday days bring crowds up Arthurs Seat, and a taxi avoids the drive up the mountain road.
access: Paths can include slopes and uneven ground, so ask the venue about accessible areas, and let us know if you need help from the car.
tips: Combine with the Arthurs Seat Eagle nearby.
School holidays are busy, so book early.
Bring a change of clothes for kids after the tube slides and tree surfing.
about: The Enchanted Adventure Garden sits near the summit of Arthurs Seat, offering hedge mazes, gardens, tube slides and tree surfing courses through the canopy. It is a popular family day out, especially during school holidays.

Families book us so the adults can relax rather than tackle the drive up Arthurs Seat. We also bring school and birthday groups, and visitors staying in Dromana, Rosebud and McCrae who would rather not move the car. With the Arthurs Seat Eagle close by, it is easy to combine both in one day. Tree surfing and the larger mazes appeal to older children and teenagers, while the gardens suit younger kids and grandparents. Groups often finish at different times, so tell us when you book if you need more than one pick-up. We can also take you down to Dromana or Rosebud for lunch afterwards.

For wheelchair users, our accessible van and Maxi WAT have four-point restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning. The Maxi WAT seats up to eight passengers without wheelchairs, ideal for families. Our drivers will help passengers from the front door to the garden entrance.

faq.q: Can you take us from the Enchanted Adventure Garden to the Arthurs Seat Eagle?
faq.a: Yes. They are close together on Arthurs Seat. Book the trips together, and we can drop you at the Eagle summit station after your visit, or collect you at the base station after your ride down. Allow time for both, as families often spend longer than planned.

faq.q: Do you have vehicles for large families going to the Enchanted Adventure Garden?
faq.a: Yes. The Maxi WAT seats up to eight without wheelchairs on board, or we can send several sedans. Let us know your group size and any prams or mobility aids when booking. If part of your group is leaving early, we can arrange two pick-ups at different times so nobody has to wait around.

name: Mornington Racecourse
description: Taxi to Mornington Racecourse for race days, functions and events. Book a sedan, Maxi or wheelchair accessible taxi home after the last race.
entrance: We drop you at the main public entrance; tell us if you have a function or members’ entry booking.
spot: Drop-off and pick-up are at the main entrance area. On busy race days we may stop where marshals direct taxis, and we will call to let you know.
parking: Race days mean drinks with friends, and a taxi gets everyone home safely after the last race.
access: Let us know if you need the wheelchair van or help from the car, and ask the racecourse about accessible viewing areas.
tips: Book your return trip before race day, as everyone leaves after the last race.
Race-day groups of up to eight can ride together in the Maxi WAT.
Tell us if you are attending a function so we drop you at the right entrance.
about: Mornington Racecourse is home to the Mornington Racing Club and hosts thoroughbred race meetings throughout the year, along with functions and events in its facilities. Feature race days draw big crowds from across the peninsula and Melbourne.

Race-goers book us so everyone can enjoy the day without a designated driver. We bring groups from Mount Martha, Mornington, Frankston and further afield, and collect them at the end of the day. Functions and events at the racecourse are another common reason for trips. Feature race days draw a dressed-up crowd, and traffic around the course builds quickly as the last race finishes. If your group is staying in different suburbs, we can arrange separate cars, or one Maxi WAT if everyone is heading the same way. Functions held at the course on non-race days are another reason we run trips here.

Race-goers who use a wheelchair can travel in the ramp-equipped van, which takes four other passengers, or the Maxi WAT, which fits two wheelchairs and six seated friends. All our wheelchair vehicles have four-point restraints. Book early for feature race days, when demand peaks.

faq.q: How do we get home from Mornington Racecourse on a big race day?
faq.a: Book your return trip before the day. Many people leave after the last race, and a booked taxi is held for your time. Tell us the number of passengers and destinations, and we can send one larger vehicle or several sedans.

faq.q: Can you bring a group to a function at Mornington Racecourse?
faq.a: Yes. Let us know the function times, guest numbers and pick-up addresses. We can arrange sedans, the wheelchair van and the Maxi WAT, and send confirmations by SMS or email. If guests are leaving at different times, we can stagger the pick-ups so nobody waits too long.

name: Point Nepean National Park
description: Taxi to Point Nepean National Park in Portsea for coastal walks, forts and the Quarantine Station. Return trips and wheelchair taxis.
entrance: We drop you at the park entrance area at the end of Point Nepean Road, or as far as private vehicles are allowed on the day.
spot: Pick-up is near the park entrance or the furthest car park vehicles can reach. Tell us where you plan to finish so we can meet you there.
parking: Car parks near the park entrance can fill in summer, and a taxi means you can walk one way and be collected without returning to the car.
access: Ask Parks Victoria about accessible paths, and let us know if you need the wheelchair van or help from the car.
tips: Plan your walk and choose a pick-up point before you set off.
Combine with lunch at Portsea afterwards.
Bring water and sun protection, as the walks are exposed.
about: Point Nepean National Park covers the tip of the Mornington Peninsula, overlooking The Rip where Port Phillip meets Bass Strait. It includes the historic Quarantine Station, military fortifications at Fort Nepean, and coastal walking tracks with views across to Queenscliff.

Visitors book us to reach the park without worrying about parking, often walking one way and being collected later. History lovers, walkers and families come for the forts and the views, and many finish with a meal at Portsea or Sorrento. History is everywhere here, from the old Quarantine Station buildings to the gun emplacements and tunnels at Fort Nepean. Allow time to explore, and choose a pick-up time that leaves room for the walk back. Weather can change quickly at the tip of the peninsula, so bring a layer even on sunny days.

Our wheelchair accessible van and Maxi WAT have four-point restraints and air-conditioning, and drivers help from door to door. Parks Victoria can tell you about accessible paths within the park. Book ahead in summer, when the southern peninsula is busiest.

faq.q: Can you drive us all the way to Fort Nepean?
faq.a: Private vehicle access within the park can be limited, and we can only go where cars are allowed on the day. We will drop you at the park entrance or the furthest car park available. Check with Parks Victoria about walking routes and any shuttle options.

faq.q: Can you pick us up from Point Nepean and take us to Portsea for lunch?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us where you will finish your visit and the time, and we will meet you there and take you to Portsea or Sorrento. You can book the trip home from lunch at the same time. Allow extra time for the walk back to your pick-up point.

name: The National Golf Club
description: Taxi to The National Golf Club at Cape Schanck for rounds, tournaments and functions. Book sedans, the Maxi or wheelchair accessible taxis.
entrance: We drop you at the clubhouse entrance; tell us which course you are playing so we head to the right clubhouse.
spot: Drop-off and pick-up are at the clubhouse. Let us know your tee time and expected finish so we can meet you on time.
parking: A post-round drink in the clubhouse is easier to enjoy when someone else is driving home.
access: Let us know about mobility needs, and ask the club about access around the clubhouse.
tips: Tell us how many golf bags you have so we send the right vehicle.
Book your return trip before your round.
The club has more than one course, so mention which one you are playing.
about: The National Golf Club is a private members’ club at Cape Schanck with several courses set among the dunes and coastal scrub of the southern peninsula. It is well regarded among golfers and hosts members, guests and tournaments.

Golfers book us to reach The National for rounds and events, especially when a post-game drink is on the cards. We also bring guests from nearby resorts and holiday homes, and run players to Melbourne Airport afterwards. Visiting players often come down from Melbourne for a day of golf, and many book us for the full return trip so they can enjoy a drink in the clubhouse. As it is a private members’ club, make sure your round is confirmed with the club before you book your taxi. We can also link your round with a stay at a nearby resort.

Our sedans suit small groups, and the Maxi WAT seats up to eight, with room for golf bags depending on numbers. For passengers using wheelchairs, the accessible van and Maxi WAT both have four-point restraints. Drivers help door to door.

faq.q: Can you fit golf bags in your taxis?
faq.a: Yes, depending on group size. Tell us how many passengers and golf bags you have when booking, and we will send a sedan or the Maxi WAT with enough room. For larger groups, we may suggest two vehicles. Tell us about any wheelchair users too.

faq.q: Can you take us from The National to Melbourne Airport after our round?
faq.a: Yes. Book your pick-up time based on your expected finish, and tell us your flight details. Allow plenty of time for traffic, and let us know about luggage and golf bags. A fixed quote is available on request for the long run to Tullamarine, and you will receive confirmation by SMS or email.

name: Moonah Links Golf
description: Taxi to Moonah Links in Fingal for golf days on the Open and Legends courses. Book golf groups, airport runs and wheelchair accessible taxis.
entrance: We drop you at the golf clubhouse; if you are staying at the resort, tell us and we will meet you at reception.
spot: We drop and collect at the clubhouse door. Let us know your tee time and expected finish so we arrive on time.
parking: Golf days often end with drinks in the clubhouse, and a taxi gets players home safely.
access: Let us know about mobility needs, and ask the club about accessible areas.
tips: Tell us how many golf bags you have when booking.
Peninsula Hot Springs is close by for a soak after your round.
Book returns before your round on weekends.
about: Moonah Links is a golf complex at Fingal with two championship courses, the Open Course and the Legends Course, set among coastal dunes. The Open Course has hosted the Australian Open, and the complex sits alongside Peppers Moonah Links Resort.

Golfers book us for social rounds, corporate days and tournaments, so that the whole group can enjoy the clubhouse afterwards. We also carry visitors staying in Rye and Sorrento, and run players to Melbourne Airport at the end of a golf trip. Corporate golf days are common here, with groups arriving in the morning and finishing with dinner or drinks. We can stagger pick-ups for players leaving at different times, and send the Maxi WAT for those heading the same way. Guests at the neighbouring resort also book us for the hot springs, the back beaches and the wineries.

Our sedans carry up to four passengers, and the Maxi WAT seats up to eight. For passengers using wheelchairs, the accessible van and Maxi WAT both have four-point restraints and air-conditioning. Book early on weekends and during tournaments.

faq.q: Can you bring a golf group to Moonah Links from Melbourne?
faq.a: Yes. Tell us how many players and golf bags you have, and we will suggest sedans or the Maxi WAT. Book your drop-off for before your tee time and your return for after the round. A fixed quote is available on request for longer trips, and you will receive confirmation by SMS or email.

faq.q: Is Moonah Links near Peninsula Hot Springs?
faq.a: Yes. The springs are a short hop from the golf course, both in Fingal. Many golfers book a soak after their round, and we can take you from the clubhouse to the springs and on home afterwards. Book the springs session first so we can time each pick-up around it.

name: Red Hill Community Market
address: Red Hill Recreation Reserve, Red Hill VIC 3937
description: Taxi to the Red Hill Community Market at the Red Hill showgrounds for local produce, crafts and food. Wheelchair taxis and pick-ups.
entrance: We drop you at the main entrance to the showgrounds on market day.
spot: Drop-off and pick-up are at the main entrance or where traffic marshals direct vehicles on the day. We will call if we need to meet you elsewhere.
parking: Market days bring heavy traffic to Red Hill, and a taxi saves queuing for a car park.
access: The market is outdoors on grass and gravel, so let us know if you need help, and ask the market about accessible routes.
tips: Check the market’s dates before booking, as it does not run every week.
Arrive early for the best produce and fewer crowds.
Combine with a Red Hill winery visit afterwards.
about: The Red Hill Community Market is one of the longest-running markets on the Mornington Peninsula, held at the Red Hill Recreation Reserve, also known as the Red Hill showgrounds. Stallholders sell local produce, crafts, plants and food, and the market draws visitors from across Melbourne.

People book us to avoid market-day traffic and parking, and to carry home their purchases. Many visitors combine a morning at the market with lunch or a tasting at a Red Hill winery. The showgrounds also host the Red Hill Show and other community events through the year. The market is a favourite outing for older residents too, and many book our wheelchair accessible van so they can browse with a carer and get home without a long walk back to a car. If you buy plants or bulky items, tell the driver at pick-up and we will help load them.

For passengers using wheelchairs, our accessible van and Maxi WAT have four-point restraints and air-conditioning. We accept MPTP cards and NDIS and aged-care accounts, and a carer can come to the market too. Drivers can carry your market bags to the vehicle and see you to your front door.

faq.q: When is the Red Hill Community Market on?
faq.a: The market runs on set dates, not every week, and the schedule can change. Please check the market’s own information before booking your taxi, then choose drop-off and pick-up times to suit. Arriving early helps you avoid the busiest part of the morning, and booking ahead is recommended on market days.

faq.q: Can you take us from the market to a Red Hill winery?
faq.a: Yes. Many cellar doors are a short drive from the showgrounds. Tell us your plans, and we can book each leg so you can enjoy a tasting without anyone driving. Check the winery’s opening hours first, and tell the driver if you have bags of produce or plants to load.

name: Frankston Arts Centre
description: Taxi to Frankston Arts Centre on Davey Street for theatre, concerts and community events. Book a return trip or wheelchair accessible taxi.
entrance: We drop you at the main entrance on Davey Street.
spot: Drop-off and pick-up are outside the main entrance. After shows, we may stop a little along the street if the kerb is busy, and we will let you know.
parking: Evening shows end at the same time, and a booked taxi saves the rush to leave the car park.
access: Let us know if you need the wheelchair van or help from the car, and ask the arts centre about accessible seating.
tips: Book your return trip for shortly after the show’s expected finish.
Arrive early to collect tickets and find your seat.
Tell us about wheelchairs when booking so we send the right vehicle.
about: Frankston Arts Centre is the City of Frankston’s performing arts centre on Davey Street, hosting theatre, music, comedy, dance and community events. Its venues include a main theatre and smaller spaces, and it is a hub for local schools and arts groups.

Theatre-goers from across the peninsula book us to get to shows without worrying about the drive home. We also bring older patrons and community groups who prefer not to drive at night, and pick up families after school concerts and dance recitals. School concerts, dance recitals and graduation nights are busy, with many families arriving and leaving at once. Booking ahead means you are not left waiting on Davey Street with tired children after a late finish. For older patrons, a door-to-door taxi makes a night at the theatre much easier, especially on cold winter evenings.

For patrons using wheelchairs, the accessible van carries one chair and four seated passengers, while the Maxi WAT carries two chairs and six seated. MPTP cards are accepted for eligible passengers, and carers travel along. Drivers walk with you from the vehicle to the foyer doors if you need a hand.

faq.q: Can you pick us up after a show at Frankston Arts Centre?
faq.a: Yes. Book your return trip for shortly after the show’s expected finish time. If the show runs late, call us and we will adjust where we can. Booking ahead means a car is set aside for your time. Tell us about any wheelchair users.

faq.q: Can a wheelchair user travel to the Frankston Arts Centre by taxi?
faq.a: Yes. Book our accessible van or Maxi WAT, and the driver will help you from your door to the entrance. Ask the arts centre about accessible seating when you book your tickets. Carers travel with the passenger, and MPTP cards are accepted for eligible passengers who hold one.

name: Melbourne Cricket Ground
description: Taxi from the Mornington Peninsula to the MCG for AFL, cricket and concerts. Book a return trip, the Maxi or a wheelchair accessible taxi.
entrance: We drop you as close to your gate as traffic and road closures allow; tell us your gate when booking.
spot: Pick-up after events is at a point agreed when you book, away from the heaviest crowds. We will call if road closures mean we need to change it.
parking: Parking around the MCG on game day is limited and slow to leave, and a taxi lets you enjoy the game without the drive home.
access: Let us know if you need the wheelchair van or help from the car, and ask the MCG about accessible seating and entry.
tips: Book your return trip before the game, and agree a pick-up point away from the main crowds.
Allow extra time for traffic before big games and concerts.
Footy groups of up to eight can share the Maxi WAT to the ground.
about: The Melbourne Cricket Ground is Australia’s best-known sporting stadium, set in Yarra Park on the edge of the city. It hosts AFL matches including the Grand Final, the Boxing Day Test and major concerts, drawing huge crowds throughout the year.

Peninsula and Frankston fans book us so they can enjoy the game without the drive home or the hunt for a car park. We also carry families with older relatives and wheelchair users who want door-to-door help rather than crowded trains. Big games often mean road closures and heavy traffic, so we plan drop-off and pick-up points with you in advance. Some fans prefer to be dropped off and walk the last stretch through Yarra Park, while others need to be as close to their gate as possible. Tell us what suits your group and we will work around event-day conditions.

Our wheelchair accessible van and Maxi WAT both have four-point restraints and air-conditioning. The Maxi WAT carries two wheelchairs plus six seated passengers, ideal for families and groups. Fixed quotes are available on request for the trip to the city and back.

faq.q: Where will you pick us up after a game at the MCG?
faq.a: Road closures and crowds change on event days, so we will agree a pick-up point with you when booking, usually a short walk from the stadium away from the heaviest traffic. We will call if we need to change it on the night.

faq.q: Can you bring a wheelchair user from the peninsula to the MCG?
faq.a: Yes. Book our accessible van or Maxi WAT, and tell us about the chair and your gate. The driver will help you to the drop-off point and secure the chair with four-point restraints. Ask the MCG about accessible seating. Carers travel with you.

name: Marvel Stadium
description: Taxi from the peninsula to Marvel Stadium in Docklands for AFL, concerts and events. Return trips, the Maxi and wheelchair taxis available.
entrance: We drop you as close to your gate as traffic allows; tell us your gate or entrance when booking.

about: Marvel Stadium is a covered stadium in Docklands with a retractable roof, hosting AFL matches, concerts and major events. It sits on the western edge of the city near Southern Cross Station.

Fans from the peninsula and Frankston book us so they can enjoy the game or concert without the drive home or the cost of parking. We also carry families with children and older relatives who prefer door-to-door help. The roof means games and concerts go ahead whatever the weather, which makes the stadium busy through winter. Leaving after a big event can be slow, with crowds heading for Southern Cross Station and cars queuing out of nearby car parks. A booked taxi with an agreed meeting point helps you avoid the worst of it, and families with young children appreciate heading straight home.

Supporters in wheelchairs can choose the accessible van, with a rear ramp and room for four others, or the hoist-equipped Maxi WAT for two chairs and six seated passengers. A carer can travel in the same vehicle, and drivers help with the walk to the drop-off point. Ask for a fixed quote if you would like to know the cost of the return trip upfront.

faq.q: Where will you pick us up after an event at Marvel Stadium?
faq.a: Road closures and crowds change on event nights, so we will agree a pick-up point with you when booking, usually a short walk from the stadium. We will call you if we need to move it on the night. Book well before match day.

faq.q: Can you take a group of friends to Marvel Stadium?
faq.a: Yes. A group of up to eight can travel together in the Maxi WAT, or we can split you across sedans. Book drop-off and return times together, and let us know your pick-up addresses. Agree a meeting point for after the event, as Docklands streets get crowded when everyone leaves at once.

about: Rod Laver Arena is the centre court of the Australian Open and one of Melbourne’s main concert venues, located in the Melbourne Park sports and entertainment precinct beside the Yarra. It hosts major international tours, sporting events and shows throughout the year.

Peninsula and Frankston residents book us for concerts and tennis, so they can enjoy the night without the drive home. We also carry families with older relatives and wheelchair users who want door-to-door help rather than navigating trams and trains. Concert nights often finish late, and the walk to a train can be long and crowded. A booked taxi with a pick-up point agreed in advance means you can head straight home to the peninsula. During the Australian Open, many fans spend a full day at Melbourne Park, so set your pick-up for after the last match you plan to see.

Our wheelchair accessible van and Maxi WAT have four-point restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning. A carer can come along to the show in the same vehicle, and NDIS and aged-care accounts are welcome. You can ask for a fixed quote for the return run between the peninsula and Melbourne Park.

faq.q: Can you pick us up after a concert at Rod Laver Arena?
faq.a: Yes. Book your return trip ahead and we will agree a pick-up point near Melbourne Park, away from the heaviest crowds. If the show runs late or roads are closed, we will call to confirm where to meet. Big concerts book out, so reserve early.

faq.q: Can you take us to the Australian Open?
faq.a: Yes. During the tournament, Melbourne Park is very busy, so allow extra time and book your trips early. Tell us your session times, and we will arrange drop-off and pick-up near the precinct. Booking ahead is strongly recommended, and fixed quotes are available on request for the return trip.

about: Flemington Racecourse is home to the Victoria Racing Club and the Melbourne Cup, run each November during the Melbourne Cup Carnival. It hosts race days throughout the year, along with functions and events.

Racegoers from the peninsula and Frankston book us so everyone in the group can enjoy the day. During Cup week, roads around Flemington are busy and pick-ups need planning, so booking ahead and agreeing a meeting point is essential. Cup week brings long days and big celebrations, and many groups book a taxi so everyone can enjoy themselves. Outside the Carnival, Flemington hosts race meetings and functions throughout the year, which are usually easier to get to. Whatever the occasion, agreeing a pick-up time and place in advance makes the end of the day far smoother.

For passengers using wheelchairs, our accessible van carries one chair and four seated passengers, while the Maxi WAT carries two chairs and six seated. Drivers help from door to door, and carers travel along. A fixed quote for the trip to Flemington and back is available on request.

faq.q: Can you take our group to Flemington for the Melbourne Cup?
faq.a: Yes. Book early, as Cup week is one of our busiest times. Tell us your group size, pick-up addresses and gate, and we will suggest sedans or the Maxi WAT. Agree a return time and pick-up point before the day.

faq.q: Where will you pick us up after the races at Flemington?
faq.a: Road closures and crowds change on big race days, so we will agree a pick-up point with you when booking, usually away from the busiest gates. We will call if we need to move it on the day. Booking ahead is essential in Cup week.

about: The Melbourne Convention and Exhibition Centre sits at South Wharf on the Yarra, hosting conferences, trade shows, consumer expos, exams and gala events. It covers a convention centre and a large exhibition centre, linked to the Pan Pacific Melbourne hotel.

People from the peninsula and Frankston book us to get to conferences, expos and graduation events without the stress of city parking. Exhibitors with equipment and visitors with mobility needs value door-to-door help. Some customers visit an expo for the day, while others need to be there for an early conference session and home again in the late afternoon. We can schedule both trips in one booking and adjust if your session runs over. For graduation ceremonies and gala dinners, families often travel together in the Maxi WAT so everyone arrives at once and nobody drives in the city.

Our wheelchair accessible van and Maxi WAT have four-point restraints and air-conditioning. The Maxi WAT carries two wheelchairs plus six seated passengers, suiting groups attending events together. If you attend events here regularly, ask us for a fixed quote.

faq.q: Which entrance will you drop us at?
faq.a: The centre has more than one entrance, so tell us the event and hall when booking. We will drop you at the closest entrance we can reach. On busy days, we may agree a nearby pick-up point for the trip home.

faq.q: Can you take us from Frankston to the convention centre for an early start?
faq.a: Yes. Book your pick-up time with allowance for peak-hour traffic, and add your return trip. You will see a fare estimate as you book, and a fixed quote is available if you ask. If you are exhibiting, mention any equipment so we send a vehicle with enough room.
